SUMMARY: On March 10, 2026, the Village adopted an ordinance annexing approximately 446.14 acres of land, known as Artistry Lakes. The County objected to the annexation because the annexation area does not meet the requirements of Section 171.043, Florida Statutes. On March 26, 2026, the County passed a resolution initiating the Conflict Resolution Procedures under Chapter 164. Florida Statutes. On February 10, 2026, after discussions with the County, the Village initiated the Interlocal Service Boundary Agreement (ISBA) process to negotiate the terms under which the subject property and adjacent properties will be annexed. The County adopted its responding resolution on February 26, 2026. While the Village approved the ISBA, the Palm Beach County Board of County Commissioners (BCC) denied it on August 26, 2026. On September 30th, 2026 the County Administrator and the Village Manager met per Ch. 164 Conflict Resolution Proceedings. Both the County Administrator and the Village Manager agreed to bring the ILA to their respective governing bodies. The County also agreed to bring the PBA to the BCC at the same time as the ILA. The Village Council approved the ILA on October 13, 2026.

SUMMARY: The TSA LEORP provides for reimbursement to airport operators for expenses incurred for the provision of law enforcement services at airport security checkpoints. The terms and conditions for participation in the TSA LEORP are set forth in the Parent Agreement. Airport operators participate in the TSA LEORP by accepting funding through Individual OTA’s, which require compliance with the Parent Agreement. At Broward College, we witness firsthand the life-changing impact of the School Readiness program. For many of our student-parents, access to affordable, high-quality childcare is not merely a support service, it is the deciding factor in whether they can persist, complete their degrees, and transition successfully into the workforce. By alleviating this critical financial burden, ELC Broward empowers parents with stability and peace of mind, enabling them to fully invest in their education and career advancement. The City of Sunrise’s investment in this initiative yields far-reaching benefits beyond individual families. It strengthens the local economy by supporting small childcare businesses and sustaining the educators who serve our youngest learners. At the same time, it ensures that children enter school socially and academically prepared laying the foundation for long-term success that benefits the entire community. Following execution of the Public Transportation Grant Agreement, staff developed a Request for Proposals for an operator and, on March 22, 2022, awarded the contract to Beefree, LLC d/b/a Freebee for On-Demand Transportation Services. Service began in September 2022 with four Tesla Model X vehicles that can accommodate up to six passengers each. The program provides first- and last-mile connectivity to other forms of mass transit and offers local transportation between hotels, businesses, restaurants, residences, and shopping destinations. These services help reduce vehicle trips, alleviate local roadway congestion, and improve parking availability. Similar to rideshare platforms such as Uber and Lyft, riders within the Western Sunrise Business and Entertainment District can request a free ride using the mobile Freebee app.

The Third Amendment to the ILA was developed in collaboration between Broward County and the Broward County City Manager’s Association (BCCMA). It included reprioritization of the current distribution of Transportation Surtax funding to Municipalities among Community Shuttle, Capital Projects, and Rehabilitation and Maintenance (R&M) Projects; a creation of a new Formula-based Funding model for R&M Projects and On-Demand Transportation during County Fiscal Years 2026 to 2032, subject to availability of Transportation Surtax funding; the development of a new means of allowing Municipalities the ability to obtain Transportation Surtax funding to be used as required local match in relation to state and federal appropriations and grants; provided Municipalities with flexibility on how each will use Formula-based Funding from the Transportation Surtax; and outlined the criteria for evaluating process, documented the allocation for municipal capital projects, and included other minor changes.

INTRODUCTION The City of Sunrise (City) has received funding from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA), and as part of the FY 21/22 Budget, funds were allocated for the City Commission Priority Projects and Programs. One of the City Commission programs that has been proposed is a "Blue Tarp" Roof Repair and Replacement Program (Program) for homesteaded single-family homes located east of Pine Island Road. It is the intent of this Program to target roof assembly repairs and roof assembly replacements for existing residential homes with "Blue Tarps." For the purpose of this Program, "Blue Tarp" is defined as any type of waterproof general-purpose tarp, of any color, that has been temporarily fastened to a damaged roof to prevent water intrusion. The purpose of this document is to establish the eligibility criteria, guidelines, and procedures, which will govern the "Blue Tarp" Roof Repair and Replacement Program for the City of Sunrise. In such situation, upon notice by either party, each party, within five (5) business days shall reduce its description of the dispute to writing and deliver it to the other party. In the event the parties cannot agree, either party may resort to court to resolve the dispute.

Description ATY Resolution - C26165 Proposal and Appendix Sole Source Sunbiz - Hoover Pumping Systems Corporation Background: The Bridges at Springtree Golf Club is a 67-acre, par 62 executive golf course, which first opened in 1972. Since that time it has undergone significant renovatio ns; however, the existing irrigation pump station has been in continuous operation for 25 years. It has now reach the end of its useful life as many of its critical components are outdated and beyond their typical 15-20 year lifespan. The irrigation pump station is a critical component of the golf course and as such, it is necessary to maintain it in peak condition to ensure business continuity and optimal operating condition year round to avoid any potential disruptions. The Bridges at Springtree Golf Club is extremely busy and remains in high demand among many City residents and visitors.

The system provides 200,000 lbs. of force to displace/cut metal materials to extricate victims involved in vehicle collisions and heavy machinery incidents. AMKUS tools are safer to handle, environmentally friendly, and perform on demand to serve our community interests during emergency incidents.

The Fire Rescue Department currently has a vehicle extrication kit on each Fire Engine; however, four are an older gas-powered Hurst model and only one is a newer AMKUS electric hydraulic rescue tool system. As part of the FY 2026 Budget process, funding was provided to replace one of the older models with a new AMKUS electric hydraulic vehicle extrication kit. To maintain operational consistency, standardization of equipment, and continuity in training and maintenance procedures, the Fire Rescue Department is requesting authorization to purchase this equipment one AMKUS electric hydraulic vehicle extrication kit to replace one of the older gas-powered models from the authorized sole source provider. We are also specifying the AMKUS electric hydraulic vehicle extrication kit in all new Fire Engine purchases to ensure operational consistency among equipment.

EXPLANATION: Congress appropriated funds through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) Community Development Block Grant - Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) Program in response to the 2023 Hurricane Idalia (DR-4734-FL) and the 2024 Hurricane Helene (DR-4828- FL). Assistance for these disasters was appropriated on December 21, 2024, by the Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act of 2025. The City of St. Petersburg (City) was allocated $159,884,000 per the Allocation Announcement Notice (90 FR 4759) published on January 16, 2025. On June 12, 2025, City Council approved the CDBG-DR Action Plan for the use of the federal grant funds (Resolution No. 2025-327) which allocated $6,000,000 to the Non-Profit Community Support Services (NPCSS) program. HUD approved the City’s Action Plan in August 2025 and executed the City’s Grant Agreement in February 2026. Through extensive public input and Unmet Needs and Mitigation Needs Assessments in the Action Plan, the City determined the need to create the Non-Profit Community Support Services (NPCSS) program to address the increased need for essential community services as a result of the qualifying disasters. This is the funding available for all three core services combined, meaning each selected organization will receive an award below this maximum amount. Outlined below are the award caps for each Core Service type: • Case Management award: up to $725,000 • Assertive Outreach award: up to $175,000 • Clinical Mental Health Services award: up to $350,000 Each organization must submit a budget that does not exceed the maximum award cap for the Core Service type(s) for which they are applying. If an organization is applying to administer multiple Core Services, the submitted budget must not exceed the combined total of both Core Service award caps. For example, if an organization applies for Case Management and Assertive Outreach, the budget cannot exceed $900,000. In this scenario, the organization must still break out the budget into sections outlining which costs are related to Case Management and which costs are related to Assertive Outreach.
